scenario: You receive a text message from a friend that says only, “Hey.”
You are handed a table at a cafe with food already placed a tiny bit off the center.
A colleague emails you to say that a meeting has been abruptly cancelled.
You notice a small typo in a document that is otherwise perfect.
Your smart thermostat drops the temperature by a single degree during the night.
You are trying to pair a wireless earbud that says it is connected but has no sound.
A neighbor’s dog starts barking at nothing in your new apartment.
You hand a half-finished sentence to a friend who stops you midway.
The printer jams after printing three pages.
Someone stands five feet away from you while looking at their phone.
You pick up a cup of coffee and spill a single bean onto your sleeve.
A subway announcement repeats the same station name twice during a stop.
You are asked to guess the price of an item at an auction without overbidding.
You are assembling flat-pack furniture with screws that do not spin.
A friend mentions their new job but does not give the company name.
You are in a group where three people speak at once.
You notice a smudge on a lens of binoculars.
Someone refers to a location by a name that is slightly off from the real one.
You find a coin in a pocket and are not certain if it has come from your wallet.
An interview question asks you to elaborate but provides no further direction.
You are told to write a ten-line reflection on a picture of a falling leaf.
A shop assistant asks for the card without asking for the exact total.
A person excuses themselves from an office meeting by saying, “I have something.”
A teacher asks you for your opinion after showing a single sentence from a book.
Two friends ask where you will go for dinner but do not suggest any locations.
You are asked to explain why you feel a hint of anxiety without any context.
You notice something in a video that is shown for only one second.
You are given a mathematical problem with extra but irrelevant numbers.
A calendar invite lists the time in an imprecise range like “sometime around three.”
Someone asks a question in a language you do not fully know and asks you to repeat it.
You are at a library and notice a book’s spine is damaged but the page count is correct.
A relative calls with a vague problem before offering a solution.
You attempt to order a specific drink but the barista reorders the ingredients unintentionally.
A message is received without any time stamp.
You feel a sudden wave of fatigue but cannot explain what triggered it.
You are asked to summarize a book that you only read two hours ago.
You carry a luggage label with your last name misspelled once.
Two people begin explaining the same history event at the same time.
You receive a cryptic email asking whether you are okay without a phrase like “Are you doing well?”
You see an advertisement that uses jargon you do not understand.
A coordinator asks you to resend the document without saying which document.
You see a street sign that points the wrong way from your intended destination.
Someone hands you a remote without ever mentioning what the device does.
You are told to think about a word for five minutes before writing it down.
A colleague stops a presentation to ask a second question without pausing the talker.
You are asked to identify a pattern in a sequence that has only three numbers.
A package arrives without a tracking label but has a fragile symbol.
Someone asks you to tailor a meal suggestion based on a single word you gave earlier.
You are standing in a silent room where one person has cracked their knuckles softly.
You are given a task to rewrite a paragraph without changing its meaning, but it already has the same meaning in the original.
